subject: Deployment mode recommendation: Hosted API vs Dedicated — follow-up & numbers requested
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina@shopline.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + numbers from our call today

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and the numbers you asked for: we ran through what we need for ShopLine's checkout personalization service. Key points: 

- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~60 requests/sec (QPS) for personalization API; peak bursts up to ~140 QPS during promotional windows (peaks last ~15 mins).
- Request shape: average prompt ~110 tokens in, average response ~160 tokens out.
- Latency target: P95 end-to-end inference latency < 120ms for user-facing calls; P99 ideally < 200ms.
- Models: evaluating open LLMs; we're flexible on exact model but want comparable quality to Llama2-70b/opt-66b.
- Data & security: must be able to place in our VPC later (may require Private / On-prem in long term).

We talked about Hosted API vs Dedicated and you asked for raw telemetry — attaching the call recording and our SLA doc (SLA_requirements_ShopLine.docx). Can you confirm: given the QPS and latency targets above, do you recommend starting on Hosted with caching/batching and a fallback to Dedicated, or should we pilot Dedicated reserved capacity from day one? Also can you send an estimated committed bandwidth / cost for a Dedicated pool that meets the numbers above?

Thanks — Lina
Lina Park
CTO, ShopLine
attachments: call-recording-20270523.mp3; SLA_requirements_ShopLine.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers from our call today

Lina — great context, thanks for the clear numbers and the SLA doc. Short answer up front: based on the profile you shared, either path can work but there are trade-offs. High-level guidance: 

- Hosted API: recommended for fast time-to-value and lower upfront spend. With Redwood's prefix caching and aggressive KV cache for repeated prompts, we can often meet P95 targets for mid-single-digit token sizes. However, sustained peak bursts to ~140 QPS with P95 <120ms for large models (70B-class) can push token-level latency unless we rely on smaller quantized variants or autoscale aggressively.

- Dedicated: recommended if ShopLine requires consistent P95/P99 across promotional peaks and wants predictable tail latency without frequent autoscale-induced cold starts. Dedicated also gives you capacity isolation and predictable throughput; fits well if you plan to push to a private VPC later.

To make a tighter recommendation I need two additional telemetry items: 
1) a 24h QPS distribution (per-minute or 1-min buckets) showing baseline vs 95th/99th percentile of requests,
2) any sample prompt/response pairs (sanitized) so we can benchmark tokenization and KV cache hit rates.

I've attached a short Deploy Mode Matrix (redwood-deploy-mode-matrix.pdf) that maps traffic/latency shapes to our recommended starting mode + pilot plan. If you want a conservative route, we can pilot Dedicated with a modest reserved pool and autoscale for peaks; if you'd rather avoid reserve costs initially we can start Hosted + a short Dedicated pilot when you hit X% of the burst traffic.

I'll loop Ben on pricing estimates for a Dedicated baseline that meets the numbers you listed.

Next steps suggested: 
- Lina: share the 24h QPS distribution and 5 example prompt/response pairs (anonymized).
- Rishi/Ben: deliver rough Dedicated-sizing + committed pricing within 48 hours.

Cheers,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Marissa — quick pricing sketch for SL-1983 given Lina's numbers: 

Assumptions: 140 QPS peak sustained for 15 min windows, avg tokens 270 total (in+out), model family approximated to 70B quantized variant.

Option A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go):
- No committed fees.
- Estimated blended token cost: ~$0.018/token-equivalent for 70B quantized path, which would translate to an approximate peak hourly cost during promos of ~$0.018 * 270 tokens * 140 QPS * 3600s ≈ $2,450/hour (note: this is burst; average hours much lower).

Option B — Dedicated Reserved Pool (monthly commit):
- Baseline pool sized for baseline 60 QPS steady with burst autoscale to handle 140 QPS with elastic buffer.
- Monthly commit estimate: $85k/mo for baseline + $25k/mo burst buffer (reserved + burst credits) — total ~ $110k/mo.
- Includes SLA, capacity isolation, and faster tail latency consistency.

Option C — Private/VPC (enterprise contract) — higher platform + support fees; we should only recommend if they need strict networking controls.

I'll prepare a formal quote if Rishi/Maria want to commit to baseline sizing; otherwise we can offer a 30-day Dedicated pilot at a discounted commit that would give ShopLine guaranteed capacity for promotional windows.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
